correspondence.component_scope: chosen western opening and unnamed feeder lake/stream chain
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is in the western unnamed lake complex northwest of Thuchonilini Lake. The original shows its southern/eastern outlet, successive smaller lakes and connecting stream east-southeast toward the northwestern approach to Thuchonilini Lake. The chosen opening, the branching lake outlines and the intervening connectors were read together, rather than assigning the nearby river name to every lake.

correspondence.component_scope: western approach, Thuchonilini Lake passage and eastern lake outlet
correspondence.finding: The stream enters the western side of the lake labeled Thuchonilini Lake. Its broad lake body connects to the eastern arm, whose outlet continues northeast into the labeled Tha-anne River and the mapped rapids. The selected route crosses this lake passage; the separately labeled Thaolintoa Lake to the north is nearby orientation, not a selected passage.

correspondence.component_scope: named upper Tha-anne reach and 65A/55D sheet-edge through-link
correspondence.finding: The east-northeast river and rapids below Thuchonilini Lake continue across the eastern boundary of 65A into the western boundary of 55D. The same eastward then southeastward corridor is labeled Tha-anne River on the originals. Both sides of the sheet seam were inspected.

correspondence.component_scope: southeast river, intermediate lake/channel reaches and southern approach to Hyde Lake
correspondence.finding: The mapped river turns south and southeast through intervening small lake expansions and rapids, then turns east and northeast into the southwestern arm of Hyde Lake. The inlet and the intermediate through-links are depicted, rather than inferred merely from the Hyde Lake label.

correspondence.component_scope: Hyde Lake crossing and eastward lower river
correspondence.finding: The selected passage crosses the lake labeled Hyde Lake, continues through its eastern extension and exits into the eastward rapids/channel below the lake. The source prose independently places Hyde Lake upstream on the Tha-anne River and distinguishes the lower Tha-anne section.

correspondence.component_scope: coastal lower course, Thlewiaza approach and actual shared estuary terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower river continues southeast into the coastal estuary, with the distinct Thlewiaza River approaching from the southwest. The mapped receiving coast is Hudson Bay. Primary fish-resource prose explicitly identifies the Tha-anne–Thlewiaza estuary and describes a several-kilometre intertidal zone. This supports the selected coastal terminal at ordinary estuary scale; no exact modern shoreline, tidal boundary or coordinate-to-bank identity is asserted. The overprinted sanctuary boundary follows portions of the lower corridor, while the river banks, adjacent reaches and estuary are still readable.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern opening and headward bends
correspondence.finding: The selected southern opening follows a mapped unnamed watercourse northwest, then north through the conspicuous westward bend and its intervening tributary joins. The CEHQ linework supports this connected opening; no official ultimate source or feeder name is assigned. The reserve report supplies broad plain and peatland context only, and its small annex thumbnail is not detailed opening evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward-to-middle junction and northward corridor
correspondence.finding: The upper selected watercourse enters the mapped northward river corridor at the substantial eastern-branch junction, then follows successive bends toward the westward turn. Nearby Yapeuthikw and Obamsca labels help distinguish the surrounding drainage but are not assigned to the whole selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle and lower Missisicabi corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the continuous northwestward river corridor through intermediate joining settings toward the provincial boundary and James Bay coast. The original carries Rivière Missisicabi at its lower reach and distinguishes the Harricana and Piscapecassy corridors to the southwest and Kitchigama to the east. These are separate neighboring river labels, not whole-group alternative names.

correspondence.component_scope: Final coastal through-link and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selection turns toward a coastal endpoint in the Hannah Bay/Little Missisicabi boundary setting. The regional map does not resolve which watercourse connects this final turn to the named Missisicabi approach. The previously read ECCC prose identifies Little Missisicabi as the southern sanctuary boundary, but no image was available to establish the connection. Neither a main-river mouth nor a separate creek identity is inferred for the final selection.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern_headward_opening
correspondence.finding: The far-eastern selected opening and its first small bends/joins lie where the regional source does not depict the complete chosen feeder. Nearby streams and lakes cannot substitute for this missing opening. No head-lake name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: upper_westward_chain
correspondence.finding: Some broader westward blue-water linework corresponds to the upper selection, but this1:2,300,000 thematic map with1:1,000,000 base does not establish all chosen lake passages and short joining segments.

correspondence.component_scope: central_obscured_connection
correspondence.finding: The093804 station-statistics panel covers or abuts the selected central path. Continuity beneath the opaque panel is not treated as observed; selected through-links and joining waterways there remain unresolved. The station number is not assigned to the selected river.

correspondence.component_scope: western_northward_bend
correspondence.finding: The source visibly follows the broader westward-to-northwestward river bend into the Lomier-side lake corridor. This supports ordinary regional route orientation, while small passage and join choices near the transition remain incompletely distinguished.

correspondence.component_scope: lac_lomier_passage
correspondence.finding: The source label Lac Lomier is on the elongated east–west waterbody traversed by the selected lower route. The lake passage and broad western continuation are geographically supported. The lake name is retained solely for this lake component and is not applied as a river or whole-system scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_river_and_actual_terminal
correspondence.finding: West of Lac Lomier the source shows a lower river turning northwest to Hudson Bay. The regional coast/territorial boundary and simplified terminal linework do not separately establish the chosen final branch and bay transition. A neighboring coastal stream is labeled Ruisseau Sucker and is not transferred to the selected river.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and Cold Creek corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern opening near the county-line/Highway 20 setting is on the mapped Cold Creek corridor. The connected creek valley continues northwest alongside Highway 20 to the mapped East Fork Russian River joining setting. The selected opening is not claimed as the ultimate or official source of Cold Creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Cold Creek to East Fork Russian River and reservoir inlet
correspondence.finding: Cold Creek meets the north-arriving East Fork corridor near the Potter Valley Road/Highway 20 setting. The selected route turns west with the mapped watercourse and enters the northern arm of Lake Mendocino, where East Fork Russian River is directly labelled. These are distinct natural reach names.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Mendocino passage and mapped dam/outlet transition
correspondence.finding: The selected route passes through the labelled reservoir from its northern inlet toward the mapped dam on its southwest side. An outlet channel connects the dam/lake setting to the Russian River corridor near The Forks, and the selected route continues south toward Ukiah. The lake, dam and outlet connection are visible in original cartography. No separate river name is imposed on the reservoir and no current release, operating rule, precise structure name or hydraulic condition is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Ukiah to Hopland and Pieta trunk
correspondence.finding: The labelled Russian River continues through the Ukiah/Talmage valley and south past the Howell, Robinson, Morrison, McNab and Crawford creek joining settings to Hopland. The Feliz/Dooley and Pieta/Cummiskey settings and intervening channel-valley passages are readable. Tributary names orient the joins and are not assigned to the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Cloverdale, Asti and Alexander Valley
correspondence.finding: The Russian River corridor continues across the county boundary, past Preston and the Big Sulphur Creek junction, through Cloverdale and Asti, then Geyserville and Alexander Valley. Direct labels and readable continuous channel geometry support the entire selected southward corridor. Small ponds, side sloughs and the separate Lake Sonoma/Dry Creek drainage do not create an additional selected through-lake requirement.

correspondence.component_scope: Healdsburg bend and Dry Creek confluence
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the Russian River past the Maacama Creek joining setting and around the pronounced Fitch Mountain/Digger Bend loop, then west to Healdsburg and south. Dry Creek joins the Russian River below Healdsburg. The coarse model cuts individual bends locally, but stays within the established connected river corridor; exact bank coincidence is neither required nor claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Windsor, lower valley and Guerneville
correspondence.finding: The connected labelled river continues south past Windsor and adjacent ponds, bends west at the lower-valley setting and passes the Mark West Creek junction. It then follows the Forest Hills/Hilton, Rio Nido and Guerneville corridor. The mapped main river remains distinct from the neighboring ponds and tributary channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Monte Rio, Austin Creek and fragment boundary
correspondence.finding: The original map follows the named Russian River from Guerneville through Monte Rio and Sheridan to the Austin Creek junction and Duncans Mills. Both selected fragments and their shared lower-river boundary lie along this continuous river corridor; no uninspected inter-fragment transfer or naming discontinuity is required.

correspondence.component_scope: Duncans Mills to actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The last selected fragment continues west along the mapped Russian River through Duncans Mills and the Sheephouse/Willow creek and Bridgehaven settings to the estuary at Jenner. The final coarse selected segment crosses the Goat Rock beach/spit a short distance south of the cartographic river-mouth opening. The actual endpoint is therefore supported as the same estuary/coastal-outlet setting, not as a pointwise mapped channel or exact mouth. The original map visibly connects the Jenner estuary to the adjacent ocean outlet; no distinct additional inland connector is required at ordinary regional scale. No precise present-day mouth, beach-crossing channel, open sandbar, tidal condition or shoreline position is claimed.
